leads.summary: Adding each raw alias between tokenized aliases changes scores of already-matching multi-term queries
leads.consequence: For the shipped trigger.capture aliases, `screen record screenrecording` matches both before and after this PR. Its contiguous name match is interrupted by the newly interposed `screen-record`, so its score falls from 38054 to 78054. In a user menu that also defines a description-matching row, that second row scores 60366 and now sorts ahead of Capture, reversing their previous order. This contradicts the limited scoring-change claim; any alias with separators followed by another alias can do it. Preserve contiguous tokenized spellings, then append raw spellings separately, or test and explicitly accept the ranking change.
leads.triage: partly in Opus final (score changes, no shipped reorder); behavioural reorder claim sent to Opus as neutral follow-up; confirmed with reproduction; published as F1

leads.summary: Related open #11580 conflicts in nameSearchText and can erase separator matches if its version wins
leads.consequence: The two PRs diverge and edit the same function: #11580 caches the old tokenized-only string, whereas this PR appends raw values. Three-way merging their exact pinned model files produces conflict markers at nameSearchText (merges/11580/merge.js:348-370). Choosing #11580's implementation makes this PR's power-menu assertion fail. Reconcile the cached computation with both tokenized and raw spellings before merging either feature; a combined model passes the five new assertions, although a full QML integration test remains needed.
leads.triage: factual; verified directly by coordinator (gh api patches of #11580, #11160, #7722); Opus had #11160/#7722; published as N1

leads.summary: New assertions miss dotted and underscored custom aliases and leaf IDs
leads.consequence: All five added assertions use a hyphen, and the only ID check fabricates install.docker-tui rather than exercising a stock ID. A plausible implementation that appends raw aliases and leaf IDs only when they contain '-' passes every new assertion but still cannot search user-declared `mail.client` or `mail_client`, which are explicitly in the PR's claimed punctuation set. Add an underscore alias/leaf and a dotted alias from a parsed user JSONC extension as positive tests, alongside a negative query.
leads.triage: dropped: rests on a contrived hyphen-only mutant; shipped menu has only hyphens; low value for public comment

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change does what the description says. Aliases and leaf ids are now found by their declared spelling, and tokenized queries still match. Two small suggestions and a note on overlapping open PRs follow.

| Query | Row | `quattro` | `quattro` + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `power-menu` | System | no match | match |
| `screen-record` | Capture | no match | match |
| `wifi-qr` | QR Code (`setup.network.qr`, shown on Wi-Fi only) | no match | match |
| `reminder-set` | Set one (`trigger.reminder.set`) | no match | match |
| `power menu`, `screen record` | same rows | match | match, same order |

**Verified:** "purely additive" holds. A generated corpus of about 2 million (query, row) pairs over the shipped menu (plus three synthetic app rows) lost no matches. Every new match is for a query containing `.`, `-` or `_`. `menu-test.sh` passes on the head and on the head applied to the current `quattro` tip, and the first new assertion fails without the change.

### Raw spellings can push some multi-word queries into a lower score tier

`nameSearchText()` now inserts each raw spelling right after its tokenized form. When a hyphenated alias or leaf id is followed by another alias, a multi-word query that includes the spaced form of the hyphenated value and continues into the next alias no longer appears in the name text as a whole. The row still matches (each term is matched separately), but `searchScore()` drops it from the name tier (40) to the lowest tier (80).

```text
Capture aliases (last two):  screen-record, screenrecording
before:  "... screen record screenrecording"                 query "screen record screenrecording" -> 38054
after:   "... screen record screen-record screenrecording"   same query                            -> 78054
```

**Impact:** small. With the shipped menu alone, no result order changed. A reorder needs another row in the same section that scores between the old and new tiers. For example, a user extension entry under `trigger.capture` whose description reads "screen record screenrecording streaming" moves from below Capture to above it for that query; a synthetic installed app whose keywords contain the same words does too. In the shipped menu the affected query restates one name in two spellings, so this is unlikely in practice. It does make the description's "scoring is unchanged except ..." slightly too strong. Other multi-word queries, such as `menu power` on System, change tier as well, with no order change in the shipped menu.

**Suggested change:** keep the tokenized parts together as before, and append the raw spellings at the end:

```js
var spelled = []
for (var j = 0; j < raw.length; j++) {
  var value = String(raw[j] || "")
  var token = searchableToken(value)
  parts.push(token)
  if (token !== value) spelled.push(value)
}
return parts.concat(spelled).join(" ").toLowerCase()
```

The old name text (ignoring a trailing space) is then a prefix of the new one, so no score can fall. On the current `quattro` tip with this variant, `menu-test.sh` passes, the corpus shows no lost matches and no lowered scores, and the reorder above disappears.

**Optional test improvement:** the two "still finds ... typed as separate words" assertions do not protect the tokenized spelling. `matchesQuery()` matches each term separately, so `power` and `menu` are both substrings of `power-menu`, and `docker tui` also matches the label "Docker TUI". A test copy of the change that keeps only the raw spellings passes every assertion in `menu-test.sh`. A ranking check placed after the existing `power menu` assertion catches it (with the raw-only version it fails with 38010 expected, 78010 actual):

```js
assertEqual(
  menu.searchScore(routed.items, routed.items['system'], 'power menu'),
  menu.searchScore(routed.items, routed.items['system'], 'power-menu'),
  'menu ranks an alias typed as separate words like the alias itself'
)
```

**Overlapping open PRs:** #11580, #11160 and #7722 each rewrite the same `return [entry.label, searchableToken(leafIdFor(entry.id)), ...]` line in `nameSearchText()`. Whichever lands later will need a manual merge that keeps the raw spellings; with #11580's version as written, the new `power-menu` assertion fails.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head, plus `menu-test.sh` and related shell tests run in an isolated sandbox on the merge-base, the head, the current `quattro` tip and the head applied to that tip. Search results and scores were computed with the shipped menu definition and a simulation of the menu's result sorting from `Menu.qml`, not observed in the running shell. The extension entry and app rows are synthetic. Overlap with other open PRs was assessed from their `MenuModel.js` changes only; full merges were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
